title: Before choosing a school-trip destination
caption: A destination shortlist starts with a school planning conversation. Agree on the learning purpose, the needs of the group and the information families will need. These three questions give teachers a practical brief to work from before comparing places to visit.

slides.label: A school planning conversation
slides.title: Before choosing a destination
slides.body: Three questions for your next school-trip planning meeting.
slides.note: Start with the students and the purpose of the trip.

slides.label: Set the brief
slides.title: Give the shortlist a purpose
slides.body: A place can be interesting and still need a closer look for this group.
items: What pace can the group manage?
What do families need to know?

slides.label: Question 01 / Learning purpose
slides.title: What should students explore in person?
slides.body: Name a question students can investigate through observation.
items: History: how does a place remember its past?
Geography: how does a city manage water?
slides.note: Plan time to discuss what students notice.

slides.label: Question 02 / Group needs
slides.title: What is manageable for this group?
slides.body: Consider age, travel experience and accessibility needs.
slides.note: Review the full day, not only the main visit.

slides.label: Question 03 / Family information
slides.title: What do families need to understand?
slides.body: Prepare clear information before asking families to commit.
items: Expected cost and what it includes.
What is confirmed and what needs checking.

slides.label: The planning takeaway
slides.title: Write the brief before the shortlist
slides.body: A useful brief connects the learning purpose, the needs of the group and the questions families will ask.
slides.note: Use it as the starting point for comparing destinations.
